subject: MedSphere — training exclusion & output ownership (DPA amendment request)
messages:
From: Tom Brady <tom.brady@medsphere.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Diane Wood <diane.wood@medsphere.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Nov 2024 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Request: DPA amendment — no-training + ownership of responses

Evelyn,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. MedSphere is generally very interested, but our legal and privacy teams have two hard requirements before we can progress to procurement: a) an explicit commitment that our interactions will not be used to train or improve models (no adaptive training or derivatives), and b) a clear statement that outputs generated by Redwood's service for our tenant are owned/controlled by MedSphere for downstream use (we need to avoid ambiguous "derivative" claims).

Can you confirm whether Redwood will sign a DPA amendment with those two commitments? If so, can you provide the proposed contractual language and any operational proof we can attach to our SOC2 review (e.g., export procedures, proof of onshore KMS, subprocessor list)?

We also need a timeline for evidence delivery and whether the no-train guarantee requires a different deployment (dedicated or private) or if it can be provided on hosted with configuration.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — Diane and I need a paper trail for our security committee.

Best,
Tom
Director of Product Security
MedSphere

[Attachment: MedSphere_DPA_request.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 15 Nov 2024 11:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: DPA amendment — no-training + ownership of responses

Evelyn / team —

Draft language we can propose (high level):
1) No Adaptive Training: "Redwood will not use Customer Content to train, fine-tune, or improve its models or other machine learning products, nor will it create persistent model artifacts derived from Customer Content."
2) Output Rights: "Customer retains ownership of Customer Content. Redwood grants Customer an exclusive, transferable, worldwide license to Outputs generated from Customer Content and will not assert ownership over such Outputs or restrict Customer's use thereof."
3) Subprocessors/Proof: include a clause committing to provide a subprocessor inventory and evidence packet (ops artifacts) within X business days of request, with onshore routing options where available.

We should also include a short operational representation that describes how the no-train promise is enforced (e.g., tenant-level toggle, ephemeral KV retention policy, disabled telemetry for learning). I'll attach a redline of the standard DPA with these clauses.

Open questions for ops/legal interplay:
- Is a technical 'no-learn' toggle sufficient, or do we gate contractual commitments to Dedicated/Private deployments for stronger guarantees?
- What evidence artifacts do we commit to (audit logs, export checklist, KMS residency attestation)?

I'll attach the redline (MedSphere_DPA_redline_v1.docx) for internal review.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: MedSphere_DPA_redline_v1.docx]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 Nov 2024 12:28:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: DPA amendment — no-training + ownership of responses

Kimberly / team —

Operational notes from infra/ops perspective:
- Hosted mode: we can provide a tenant-level "no-learn" configuration that disables model updates, telemetry ingestion for model improvement, and prefixes any captured tensors for immediate GC. However, hosted customers share multi-tenant model binaries, so absolute mathematical guarantees vs. all future training versions are limited unless we isolate weights.
- Dedicated pools: stronger guarantees. With Dedicated capacity we can run inference on isolated GPU pools and disable aggregation/telemetry at the host level.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): strongest — full control, KMS residency, and no crossover with other customers.

Evidence we can reasonably provide within 7 business days:
- Subprocessor inventory and certifications list (exportable CSV)
- KMS residency attestation for the regions requested (signed statement)
- Ops-proof packet (we will assemble a short PDF with config snapshots, retention settings, and export checklist) — see ops-proof-summary.pdf (attached).

Caveats:
- If customer requires a contractual promise that no future Redwood model trained internally will ever have exposure to their data (cryptographic guarantee), we should route to Dedicated/Private and add language limiting Redwood's use to internal-only debugging telemetry stripped for training.
- For Outputs ownership, there's no technical enforcement needed — that's contractual, but we can include logging that maps request IDs to tenant IDs to support provenance if a dispute arises.

Happy to demo the evidence packet to MedSphere ops/security. Marissa, I can drop a 30-minute tech walkthrough next Tue (11/19) if they want.

Thanks,
Karthik
VP, Platform Operations

[Attachment: ops-proof-summary.pdf]

- Evidence: the ops packet should include at least one sample export workflow (SFTP + manifest), and an attestation that KMS keys for our tenant can be provisioned onshore (US-East) if required.

If you can provide those three items and a short call on 11/19, procurement should be able to push to signature.

Best,
Tom
